question: If the mass of a football is 3 kg, then what would be its weight on the earth? (Given, = 9.8 m s⁻²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**29.4 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mass of the football is given as 3 kg.
 
• The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is 9.8 m/s².
 
• Weight is calculated using the formula: Weight (W) = Mass (m) × Acceleration due to gravity (g).
 
• Substituting the values, W = 3 kg × 9.8 m/s².
 
• The weight of the football on Earth is 29.4 N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass and Weight:**

 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, typically measured in kilograms (kg).
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object, measured in Newtons (N).
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force:**
 
 
• Gravitational force is the attractive force between two masses.
 
• On Earth, this force is quantified as 9.8 m/s².
 
 
 
• **Formula for Weight:**
 
 
• The formula to calculate weight is W = m × g.
 
• Here, W represents weight, m represents mass, and g represents the gravitational force.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gravity:**
 
 
• Gravity keeps planets in orbit around the sun.
 
• It gives weight to physical objects and is responsible for the free fall of objects.
